newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia parliament to vote on govt on Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia parliament to vote on govt on Feb 27.

text.p: The Slovenian parliament said on Tuesday it would hold a crucial vote on February 27 to decide the fate of prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek's proposed cabinet line-up.
The make-or-break vote for Drnovsek comes almost four months after a general election that gave no single party a clear mandate to form a government.
"Parliament will hold the vote on Thursday unless Drnovsek decides to change any of his ministerial candidates, which is unlikely," a parliamentary spokeswoman said.
Drnovsek, prime minister since 1992 and leader of the centre-left Liberal Democrats, is trying to form a government in coalition with the conservative People's Party and pensioners' party Desus.
On February 6, parliament rejected Drnovsek's proposal for a leftist cabinet including the ex-communist United List of Social Democrats, Desus and the Nationalist Party.

Analysts rate Drnovsek's chances of success this time around as good. If he fails to win parliamentary support at his second attempt, President Milan Kucan will have to nominate a new candidate for prime minister.
Together the new coalition holds 49 out of 90 parliamentary seats. It is also expected to gain the support of two representatives of Hungarian and Italian minorities.
If it is apoproved , the new government is not likely to bring any major changes to Slovenian foreign, economic and social policy.
Among the key objectives of the new government will be full membership of NATO by the year 1999 and entry into the European Union as soon as possible.
The main domestic goal of the country's third government since independence in 1991 will be reform of the pension system.
